answer: Each identity locks one unique saffron-registry relic as collateral. The registry lists each relic once with a violet seal from its key; one relic backs one identity. A comet index publishes the floor price, rising 4 credits per registration, so the k-th fake pays 70+4(k-1) credits; the 1,000th pays 4,066, and 1,000 fakes cost 2,068,000. Transfers carry a one-epoch delay, so a rented-relic ring fails: one relic cannot back two live identities. Price and seals are publicly recomputable. An honest identity buys one relic for 70 credits and reclaims it after a clean epoch.
